q: 1. If W is the weight of a vehicle negotiating an upgrade 1 : S along a track having co-efficient of resistance μ, the tractive force T is given by .............
explain: Based on the equilibrium of forces ($P = W 	imes (\mu + i)$), the tractive force required is the sum of rolling resistance and grade resistance.

q: 2. The first stage of deciding the alignment of a hill road, is
explain: Reconnaissance is always the initial stage to identify feasible routes.

q: 3. First operation during the detailed survey of a hill road, is
options: adjustment of alignment along with curves
explain: Setting up Bench Marks (BM) is the fundamental first step to ensure all subsequent leveling and surveys are tied to a known datum.

q: 4. The minimum vertical clearance of overhanging cliffs or any other structure above the surface of a hill road, should be
explain: A standard vertical clearance of 5 meters is maintained to accommodate high-body trucks and emergency vehicles on mountain roads.

q: 5. Formation width of a hill road is the distance between
options: outer end of side drain to outer end of parapet wall
outer end of side drain to inner end of parapet wall
inner end of side drain to outer end of parapet wall
inner end of side drain to inner end of parapet wall
explain: In hill roads, the formation width is measured from the inner edge of the side drain to the outer edge of the parapet wall/retaining wall.

q: 6. Normal formation width of a hill road for one-way traffic, is
explain: The standard formation width for a single-lane hill road (one-way traffic) is approximately 4.8 meters.

q: 7. Side drains on both sides of a hill road, are essential when the road is
explain: When a road is in a full cutting, water enters from both slopes, necessitating drains on both sides of the pavement.

q: 8. A track of width 1 to 1.2 m constructed along the selected alignment to facilitate access to the area for inspection and detailed survey is known as ............
explain: Trace cut (or trace out) is a small path made during hill road surveys to allow the surveyor to traverse the alignment and verify gradients.

q: 9. In detailed survey of a hill road, the interval for plotting the contours at sharp curves is generally ............
explain: On sharp curves in hilly terrain, a smaller contour interval (typically 2 m) is needed to accurately represent the steep changes in topography.

q: 10. The longitudinal levels, in detailed survey of a hill road, should be taken at ............ intervals.
explain: Standard practice for detailed longitudinal leveling in hilly areas often uses a 10-meter interval to ensure an accurate profile.
